newsitem.title: FRANCE: Thomson-CSF says pleased with sale terms.
newsitem.headline: Thomson-CSF says pleased with sale terms.

text.p: French defence electronics firm Thomson-CSF said on Wednesday it was pleased with the terms of its privatisation, which addressed its main concerns.
The French government announced earlier on Wednesday that it would privatise Thomson through a private placement accompanied by a book of terms and conditions.
"The management of Thomson-CSF takes note of this decision and is pleased that it answers some essential concerns of Thomson-CSF," a spokesman told Reuters shortly after the announcement.
The spokesman said Thomson management was pleased because the government said Thomson-CSF is meant to become a world-scale defence electronics company.

Thomson-CSF also welcomed the government's statement that its strategic interests would be protected by the government's holding of a "golden share" that would protect the company from being dismantled.
The government also said it would protect Thomson-CSF's strategic and commercial interests throughout the process.

The Thomson-CSF spokesman said that the company was pleased that employees would have access to the share capital of Thomson under terms similar to those which would have been available if the company had been privatised through a public share offer.
The spokesman said he was also pleased by the government's statement that the company would be closely associated with all stages of the procedure.
The spokesman added that it hoped the privatisation would take place as quickly as possible.
"We hope the calendar of the sale will be as short as possible," he said, adding that the worldwide defence sector was rapidly consolidating and that France could not afford to wait much longer.
